They also requested that the DNA and forensic reports be shared with the family.
Speaking at a press conference at the National Press Club in Islamabad, the victim’s brother, Fahad Javed, stated that the brutality with which Hina Javed was murdered was beyond description.

The body was shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital for postmortem examination, while a case was registered against the suspects under relevant sections of the law at Bargai police station.

Jehangir Khan, 79, father of the deceased woman, told Bargai police that his son-in-law, Gul Nawar Khan, was abroad and his daughter had been living in a rented house in the Kotka Amin area of Sra Darga.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority intensifies citywide cleanliness drive
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has intensified its citywide cleanliness drive to improve sanitation, remove waste and maintain public spaces, roads, green belts and parks in a clean and hygienic condition.

Chairman Sohail Ashraf has stressed the importance of keeping Islamabad clean, green and pollution-free, saying a well-maintained capital was essential for public health, environmental sustainability and the quality of life of residents.
The authority said maintaining a clean Islamabad was a shared responsibility and reaffirmed its commitment to improving municipal services and environmental management across the capital.

stories.title: PM orders probe into vaccine procurement for pilgrims
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an inquiry into the procurement of meningococcal meningitis and influenza vaccines by Border Health Services-Pakistan under a public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement for pilgrims and overseas job seekers.

According to a notification issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, a five-member committee headed by the secretary of the Cabinet Division has been constituted to examine the procurement process and determine whether it complied with applicable rules and procedures.

The inquiry comes after questions were raised over the procurement process for the two vaccines under the PPP arrangement, with concerns relating to its legal basis, the bidding process, financial implications and compliance with public procurement requirements.

summary: KARACHI: Pakistan’s first nationally representative mental health survey has shown that nearly one in three adults is living with a diagnosable mental and behavioural disorder, highlighting a major public health challenge affecting millions of people across the country.

Interviews of more than 2,000 male and female candidates shortlisted for the recruitment process are currently underway at the Central Police Office in Gilgit.

stories.title: Bar council to observe strike against governor’s rule tomorrow
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council (KPBC) on Saturday declared the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the province unconstitutional and undemocratic, and announced a province-wide strike on Oct 19 (Monday).

Mr Khan said the council constituted a lawyers’ panel to file a constitutional petition in the High Court against the imposition of emergency in the province, so that the court could hear it, along with other petitions on the matter, on Oct 20.

stories.title: Ram Leela Temple sealed amid demolition fears
summary: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: The authorities here on Saturday locked and sealed the historic Ram Leela Temple in Rahim Bazaar days after civil society activists intervened to stop demolition of the heritage building for construction of a commercial plaza at the site.
The latest development came as civil society representatives and members of the Hindu community held a joint meeting to discuss the reported move to demolish the temple.

They expressed concern over any move to demolish the temple and said civil society, the business community, writers and heritage advocates would resist any action that could damage the city’s historical heritage.

stories.title: Education dept orders safety audit of school buildings

Assistant commissioner (headquarters) Adnan Mumtaz Khattak and members of the inspection committee visited several government and private schools in Swabi tehsil to review the condition of their buildings and security arrangements.

stories.title: Islamabad reports 42 dengue cases so far this year
summary: ISLAMABAD: The District Health Office has intensified dengue surveillance across the capital after 42 cases were reported in Islamabad since January, with authorities focusing particularly on identifying hotspots and high-risk areas.
Anti-dengue teams conducted 382,452 surveillance and control activities across Islamabad during October.

The District Health Office said continuous field surveillance, timely identification and elimination of mosquito-breeding sites, and regular monitoring of hotspots were essential to keeping dengue transmission under control.

stories.title: Auto loans rise despite sales slump
summary: KARACHI: Despite a sales slowdown, outstanding car loans rose for the 22nd consecutive month to Rs407 billion in September from Rs393.3bn in August, data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) showed.
However, cumulative auto sales rose by 19pc to 50,480 units in 1QFY27.

Topline Securities Chief Executive Mohammed Sohail said auto financing is likely to rise, but more slowly, amid uncertainty over the new auto policy and rising borrowing costs, as KIBOR (Karachi interbank offered rate) has edged higher over the last few weeks.

stories.title: One dead as earthquake jolts Khuzdar
summary: KHUZDAR: A strong earthquake measuring 5.9 on the Richter scale struck Khuzdar and surrounding areas on Saturday, killing one person and damaging several mud houses.
Officials said the tremors were felt at 10:07am, prompting residents to leave their homes and seek refuge in open areas amid widespread panic.
According to official sources, a rock fell from a nearby mountain in Anari, in the Besar area of Naal, and struck Abdul Rahim, son of Qamaruddin and a resident of Wadh, killing him on the spot.

stories.title: Editors’ body elects president, general secretary
summary: KARACHI: Azhar Abbas and Tariq Mahmood were elected as president and general secretary, respectively, of the Association of Electronic Media Editors and News Directors (AEMEND) on Saturday.

According to a press release, the association also elected Muhammad Usman and Mian Tahir as vice presidents, Rehan Ahmed and Nadeem Jamal as joint secretaries, and Shahab Mahmood as finance secretary.
The general council of AEMEND, in meetings held in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad, also elected the remaining members of the executive committee.

stories.title: Kundi moves to curb dengue as cases surge
summary: An important high-level meeting was held under the chairmanship of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to review the dengue situation in the province, assess measures to prevent its further spread and evaluate the overall anti-dengue response.

Officials gave the Governor a detailed briefing on the latest dengue statistics, the implementation status of the anti-dengue action plan, the functioning of the reporting and surveillance system, and other steps being taken to contain the disease.

The Governor emphasised that the resources required by district administrations for an effective anti-dengue campaign must be provided on a priority basis so that the spread of the epidemic can be checked and the public protected from its harmful effects.

stories.title: Peshawar pilot dies in plane crash
summary: Another pilot from the well-known Qazi family, long associated with the Peshawar Flying Club, has lost his life in a microlight aircraft accident.
The tragic incident has cast a shadow of grief over the Qazi family and the wider community in Landi Arbab, Peshawar, from where the late pilot hailed.

It may be recalled that the renowned Qazi family of Peshawar (Landi Arbab) has a history of passion for amateur aviation, manufacturing gliders, and piloting aircraft, but this pursuit has unfortunately resulted in multiple tragic and fatal accidents rather than injuries.
